SokoIow Podlaski New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Sokołów Podlaski, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Sokołów Podlaski developed from the 16th or 17th century, reaching 7,745 people (70 percent) by 1910; most were murdered by the Germans at Treblinka in 1942. This cemetery's land was purchased in 1920, and per the town's own memorial book, it was established about 50 years before the community's extermination; a funeral house and fence, the latter financed by the American Jewish Joint Distribution Committee, stood at the entrance before WWII. The site was destroyed during the war and further degraded afterward, used as a gravel mine and garbage dump, before authorities formally closed it in 1963 and designated the land for other purposes; a 1991 intervention by the Provincial Office in Siedlce led to leveling and an information sign prohibiting further gravel extraction.
